diagnosis: requireToken() in server.mjs gates every /api/smart-files/* route on ONE shared secret (SMART_FILES_SERVICE_TOKEN) with no caller-scope check at all. Writes are already scoped via resolveWriteScope + assertFolderInScope (QA persona -> orgId, or explicit instrument scopeId). Reads (listFolders, listFolderFiles, readDocument, listPlacements, getBlob) take no caller argument -- the transaction contract names this exact asymmetry as the program's governing defect class.

designDecision.chosen: A read-only caller-identity model: SMART_FILES_SERVICE_TOKENS, a JSON grant list (token -> [{scopeType, scopeId}]), checked per-route against the RESOURCE's actual scope (folder's own scope_type/scope_id, entityId's parsed scope, or a blob's scope via the document(s) citing it). '*' accepted in either field but never defaulted -- an unconfigured environment reads nothing. The existing write/personas/share gate (single shared token) is left completely unchanged.
designDecision.rejectedAlternative1: Trust a client-supplied orgId/userId query param on reads, mirroring the write path's persona resolution. Rejected: a GET query param is caller-controlled and trivially spoofable -- it would let any holder of the shared write token claim to be any tenant on reads, which is not a real entitlement check.
designDecision.rejectedAlternative2: Make the existing single SMART_FILES_SERVICE_TOKEN itself tenant-bound (one secret per tenant, breaking the shared-secret model). Rejected for THIS pass: production's existing consumers (QA UI BFF, Dashboards, plan-review) all currently share ONE secret across multiple tenants (icc-demo/acme/empressa/template-city/g58-probe, per scope_roundtrip_probe.mjs's own test shape) -- narrowing that secret today would break every existing integration in the same change that closes the read defect, conflating two different-risk changes. Deferred as a named follow-up (see whatRemainsOpen in the close artifact), not silently dropped.
designDecision.backwardCompatibilityCall: The legacy SMART_FILES_SERVICE_TOKEN is NOT auto-promoted to a blanket read grant by the code. Where an operator wants existing behavior preserved (CI, and this session's production deploy), that is an EXPLICIT, visible grant entry ({scopeType: '*', scopeId: '*'}) in SMART_FILES_SERVICE_TOKENS, satisfying ENFORCEMENT.md's 'degradation permitted only when declared' rule rather than reintroducing the defect as a silent default.
